# Complete Field Reference (generated — do not edit by hand)

**Generated by `spec/tools/gen_field_reference.py` from the `spec/schemas/*.schema.json` bytes.** This document is the SCH-2 "complete field reference": the schema-embedded `description` strings are the normative reference, and this file renders every one of them — one row per field definition, including nested fields, array element fields, map values, and `$defs`. CI (`spec/tests/test_field_reference.py`) asserts (1) 100% description coverage in the schemas, (2) that regenerating this file is byte-identical to the committed copy and covers every schema property (so schema/doc drift fails loudly), and (3) reverse-drift: every backticked field path in the curated IC-1..IC-6 field tables names a real schema property. The curated IC docs remain the architecture narrative; THIS file is the exhaustive reference. Regenerate after any schema change: `.venv/bin/python spec/tools/gen_field_reference.py`.

Required column: `required` (unconditional), `conditional` (required only inside an `if/then` branch — e.g. the IC-3 `intent_kind` seam), `optional`, `map value` (schema of every value of a map field), `definition` (a named `$defs` building block).

## `action/v1` — `spec/schemas/action.v1.schema.json`

The agent's decision for one turn (IC-3): a signed target-position vector plus optional execution tolerance, rationale, and telemetry. This is the WIRE form, tuned for LLM ergonomics: target leverage values are decimal STRINGS (or bare JSON integers), never fractional JSON numbers - a JSON number with a fractional part is rejected with reason float_target, so no float ever enters a money path (DET-2/DET-4). The engine canonicalizes to integer lev_1e4 in ActionParsed; only that canonical form is hashed. Leverage-cap/turnover/kill-switch limits are deliberately NOT validated here: a well-formed over-limit action parses successfully and is then blocked by a recorded RiskCheck gate, preserving attempted-vs-executed evidence (SAFE-1).

| Field path | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | const `"action/v1"` | required | Schema name and major version of this document. |
| `intent_kind` | enum: `"leverage_target"` | optional | Optional intent discriminator (the IC-3 extensibility seam, applied at the M0 audit). Absence means 'leverage_target' - every v1 trading action is a leverage-target intent, and `target` is conditionally required exactly when intent_kind is 'leverage_target' or absent (the allOf/if/then above; vacuous truth of the if-schema when the member is absent makes absence equivalent to the const). This enum is on the additive-tolerant list (VERSIONING.md): a future non-trading intent kind (e.g. a commerce 'purchase_intent' carrying an AP2-style cart) arrives as a new enum member with its own conditionally-required payload branch - a MINOR bump, not an action/v2 major. The engine canonicalizes the discriminator into the hashed parsed form (ActionParsed.intent_kind, constant 'leverage_target' for every trading action), so determinism is unaffected. |
| `target` | object (map) | conditional | Map: market alias (as shown in the observation, e.g. 'BTC') -> signed target leverage on NAV. Sign = direction (negative = short), '0' = flat, magnitude = leverage multiple. Example: {"BTC": "-1.5"} = short 1.5x NAV. This is the entire action space: target positions, not raw orders. |
| `target.*` | (anyOf variants) | map value | Target leverage: a decimal string with at most 4 fractional digits (e.g. "1.5", "-0.25", "0") or a bare JSON integer. Parsed EXACTLY (decimal re-parse of the raw text, never via binary float) to an integer in 1e-4 leverage units ("1.5" -> 15000). Fractional JSON numbers are schema-invalid by construction. |
| `max_slippage_bps` | integer | optional | Optional. Maximum acceptable modeled slippage versus the next-bar-open reference price, in integer basis points (agent-facing bps for ergonomics; stored engine-side as slippage_1e8, 1 bp = 10000 in 1e-8 units - exact conversion). Orders whose modeled slippage exceeds this are cancelled with reason max_slippage_exceeded. |
| `comment` | string | optional | Optional free-text rationale. Never interpreted by the engine. It is NOT copied into the canonical parsed action: the verbatim response bytes (which contain it) are content-addressed into raw/, keeping rationale redactable under the share profile without touching chained records. |
| `usage` | object | optional | Optional self-reported token usage; copied by the harness into AgentResponded.token_usage. Advisory telemetry, never validated, excluded from the canonical parsed action (it is telemetry, not intent). |
| `usage.input_tokens` | integer | optional | Agent-reported input/prompt tokens consumed for this decision. |
| `usage.output_tokens` | integer | optional | Agent-reported output/completion tokens produced for this decision. |
| `ext` | object (map) | optional | Sanctioned extension point (see VERSIONING.md): engine-ignored, recorded verbatim in raw/ only (not in canonical parsed form). Keys SHOULD be reverse-DNS or x_-prefixed; values are constrained by schema to JCS-safe types with no fractional numbers ($defs/ext_value). |
| `$defs/ext_value` | (anyOf variants) | definition | JCS-safe extension value (DET-2): null, boolean, string, integer within the I-JSON exact range +/-(2^53-1), or arrays/objects of the same, recursively. A JSON number with a fractional part (e.g. 1.5) is schema-INVALID here - ext contents ride into hashed documents as-is, and no fractional number may enter a hashed document. Boundary note: JSON Schema's 'integer' type admits a mathematically-integral literal such as 1.0; the CI instance scan (float-rejecting JSON parse, see VERSIONING.md) closes that remaining lexical gap. |

## `agent_manifest/v1` — `spec/schemas/agent_manifest.v1.schema.json`

Attribution record for WHO decided: the agent's identity, adapter, egress allowlist, and frozen inference configuration. Chained via bundle_manifest.agent_manifest_sha256 and the chain genesis. Secret-free BY CONSTRUCTION (SEC-1): no field in this schema can legally hold a credential - endpoint DOMAINS not URLs-with-tokens, prompt HASH not prompt text, scalar-only inference params (decimals as strings; this manifest is hashed, so the no-floats rule applies to it like everything else).

| Field path | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | const `"agent_manifest/v1"` | required | Schema name and major version of this document. |
| `name` | string | required | Human-readable agent name chosen by the operator, e.g. 'baseline-flat' or 'my-llm-agent'. |
| `adapter` | enum: `"http"` \| `"in_process"` | required | IC-6 transport: HTTP container (V1 canonical) or in-process scripted reference agent. 'mcp' is reserved post-V1. |
| `model_id` | string | required | Model identifier as invoked/billed (e.g. provider model slug); 'none' for scripted agents. Attribution: who decided. |
| `endpoint_domains` | array of string | required | EXHAUSTIVE egress allowlist driving the sandbox lockdown (ISO-2): only these domains are reachable from the agent container; every other attempt is refused AND recorded as an EgressBlocked event. Empty array = fully offline agent. Items are bare hostnames only (pattern-enforced): a URL-with-embedded-token cannot legally appear here. |
| `inference_params` | object (map) | required | Inference settings verbatim, scalar values only. Decimal-valued params (e.g. temperature) MUST be decimal strings ('0.7'), never JSON numbers with fractional parts - this document is hashed. |
| `inference_params.*` | string \| integer \| boolean | map value | Scalar setting value; decimals as strings. |
| `prompt_sha256` | string \| null | required | SHA-256 of the system/base prompt bytes - configuration commitment without forced disclosure (prompt text itself is user-side and optional). Null when the agent has no prompt (scripted agents). |
| `agent_version` | string \| null | required | Free-form agent code version string, or null. |
| `image_sha256` | string \| null | required | Pinned Docker image digest of the agent container ('sha256:...'); null for in-process scripted agents. Reproducibility artifact. |
| `declared_by` | string | optional | Optional free-text attribution of who declared this manifest (operator handle). The 'principal' slot of a commerce mandate. |
| `ext` | object (map) | optional | Sanctioned extension point (see VERSIONING.md). Hashed as-is; values are constrained by schema to JCS-safe types with no fractional numbers ($defs/ext_value), and never credentials. |
| `$defs/ext_value` | (anyOf variants) | definition | JCS-safe extension value (DET-2): null, boolean, string, integer within the I-JSON exact range +/-(2^53-1), or arrays/objects of the same, recursively. A JSON number with a fractional part (e.g. 1.5) is schema-INVALID here - ext contents ride into hashed documents as-is, and no fractional number may enter a hashed document. Boundary note: JSON Schema's 'integer' type admits a mathematically-integral literal such as 1.0; the CI instance scan (float-rejecting JSON parse, see VERSIONING.md) closes that remaining lexical gap. |

## `bar_row/v1` — `spec/schemas/bar_row.v1.schema.json`

One OHLCV bar as a JSONL line inside a pack series file. The same row shape serves all three never-conflated price series (trade, mark, index); the series role is declared file-level in pack_manifest.files[].role, so rows carry no per-row schema field (bulk-data exception to the self-description rule; see VERSIONING.md). All prices are integer ticks (multiply by the market's tick_size_micro for micro-quote units). All timestamps are real UTC epoch-milliseconds in pack files; the observation builder rebases them before an agent ever sees them.

| Field path | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ts` | integer | required | Bar OPEN time, UTC epoch-milliseconds. |
| `available_at` | integer | required | Instant this row becomes observable = bar CLOSE time (ts + bar interval), UTC epoch-milliseconds. The point-in-time isolation key: an observation at virtual clock T may include only rows with available_at <= T (ISO-1). Stored per-row (not derived) so leakage property tests and the poison-row fixture operate on stored bytes. |
| `o` | integer | required | Open price in integer ticks (tick size in the pack manifest's market descriptor, tick_size_micro). |
| `h` | integer | required | High price in integer ticks. On the mark series this drives the intra-bar liquidation check for shorts (MATH-3). |
| `l` | integer | required | Low price in integer ticks. On the mark series this drives the intra-bar liquidation check for longs (MATH-3). |
| `c` | integer | required | Close price in integer ticks. |
| `v_base_1e8` | integer | required | Bar volume in 1e-8 base-asset units (e.g. satoshi for BTC). Feeds the participation cap on the trade series; 0 is permitted and expected on mark/index series (one row shape, three streams, one parser). |

## `bundle_manifest/v1` — `spec/schemas/bundle_manifest.v1.schema.json`

Identity of one run's evidence bundle, written ONCE at run start and never mutated (immutability beats a mutable status flag; completeness is signaled by chain.json presence + the EpisodeEnd sentinel). Pins the pack (by content hash), the agent (by manifest hash), the engine (exact semver - replay refuses any mismatch, DET-6), and the run configuration (inlined here so the whole replay input is one hashed document). Contains the single permitted wall-clock read (created_at_ms: recorded, never consumed) and the observation time-rebase offset (recorded, never observable by the agent).

| Field path | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | const `"bundle_manifest/v1"` | required | Schema name and major version of this document. |
| `run_id` | string | required | Harness-generated random run identifier. Identity, not computation: allowed entropy because it never enters the replay function's economics. |
| `episode_id` | string | required | The opaque episode id shown to the agent (observation.episode.episode_id). Recorded here so the bundle discloses the mapping the agent never sees. |
| `created_at_ms` | integer | required | Harness wall clock at run start, UTC epoch-ms. THE single permitted wall-clock read in the system: recorded, never consumed (DET-4). |
| `pack` | object | required | Which pack, pinned by content: the auditor's link from evidence to data. Replay refuses a pack whose recomputed content hash differs. |
| `pack.pack_id` | string | required | Pack slug, e.g. 'covid-2020' (operator-side; never in observations). |
| `pack.content_hash` | string | required | pack_manifest.content_hash of the pack used. |
| `pack.manifest_sha256` | string | required | SHA-256 of the pack's manifest.json bytes. |
| `agent_manifest_sha256` | string | required | SHA-256 of agent_manifest.json bytes - manifest contents are covered by the chain via this indirection. |
| `engine_version` | string | required | Exact engine/package semver that produced this bundle. tradeevolve replay REQUIRES equality; mismatch is a refusal naming both values, never silent best-effort (DET-6). |
| `spec_versions` | object (map) | required | Map: schema name -> full version used (e.g. {'observation/v1': '1.0.0'}). The compatibility surface replay checks; sourced from spec/schemas/VERSIONS.json at run time. |
| `spec_versions.*` | string | map value | Full semver of the named schema. |
| `time_rebase_offset_ms` | integer | required | Epoch-ms subtracted from real time to produce every observation timestamp: the largest whole multiple of 604800000 (one week) <= pack window start. Preserves time-of-day and weekday, destroys the calendar date (ISO-4). Recorded here for auditors; never observable by the agent (ISO-3). |
| `run_config` | object | required | The run's operator configuration, inlined (rather than a separate file) so the complete replay input is pinned by this one hashed document. The ECONOMIC SEED IS COMPLETE here: starting_nav_micro, the gross leverage cap, the drawdown kill-switch threshold, and the turnover cap are all recorded per run (DET-1/DET-3: replay is a pure function of pack bytes + this object + recorded events; no hidden inputs). Effective-lookback rule: lookback values win over pack defaults when non-null. |
| `run_config.starting_nav_micro` | integer | required | Starting account capital (NAV at bar 0) in micro-quote units. Part of the frozen replay input: ledger bar-0 NAV and metrics net_return_1e8 are seeded by it, so it MUST be pinned here (DET-1/DET-3). V1 CLI default: 10000000000 (10,000 USDT). |
| `run_config.leverage_cap_gross_lev_1e4` | integer | required | Account-wide gross leverage cap (sum of \|per-market target\|) in 1e-4 units, enforced as the lev-gross RiskCheck gate. Protocol default 30000 (3x); recorded per run like turnover_cap_1e8 so every gate limit that appears in observation.risk.constraints exists in this hashed document (SAFE-1). |
| `run_config.drawdown_kill_switch_1e8` | integer | required | Episode peak-to-trough drawdown threshold in 1e-8 units at which the kill switch flattens all positions (SAFE-3). Protocol default 20000000 (20%); recorded per run so the drawdown-ks constraint limit is pinned in the replay input, matching turnover_cap_1e8's treatment. |
| `run_config.lookback_bars` | integer \| null | required | Observation trade-bar lookback depth; null = use pack default_lookback.bars. The operator pays the token bill, so the operator's config wins. |
| `run_config.funding_prints` | integer \| null | required | Observation funding-print lookback; null = use pack default_lookback.funding_prints. |
| `run_config.response_deadline_ms` | integer | required | Per-attempt agent response budget (IC-6), echoed to the agent in observation.episode.response_deadline_ms. Default 120000. Lives in run config, not the agent manifest: it is an operator budget decision, not an agent attribute. |
| `run_config.seed` | integer | required | Recorded seed for any permitted randomness (V1 engine uses none; the field exists so any future seeded generator is recorded, DET-4). |
| `run_config.cost_profiles` | array of string | required | Cost profiles simulated and stored. V1: ['primary','stress_2x'] - both mandatory so no headline can exist only under the optimistic profile (MATH-5). |
| `run_config.turnover_cap_1e8` | integer \| null | required | Episode turnover cap (cumulative traded notional / starting NAV, 1e-8 units); null = uncapped (no turnover constraint row appears in observations). |
| `host` | object | required | Informational host provenance; explicitly OUTSIDE the determinism domain - results must not depend on it (DET-3). |
| `host.os` | string | required | Operating system, e.g. 'linux', 'darwin'. |
| `host.arch` | string | required | CPU architecture, e.g. 'arm64', 'x86_64'. |
| `host.python` | string | required | Python version string. |
| `ext` | object (map) | optional | Sanctioned extension point (see VERSIONING.md). Hashed as-is; values are constrained by schema to JCS-safe types with no fractional numbers ($defs/ext_value). |
| `$defs/ext_value` | (anyOf variants) | definition | JCS-safe extension value (DET-2): null, boolean, string, integer within the I-JSON exact range +/-(2^53-1), or arrays/objects of the same, recursively. A JSON number with a fractional part (e.g. 1.5) is schema-INVALID here - ext contents ride into hashed documents as-is, and no fractional number may enter a hashed document. Boundary note: JSON Schema's 'integer' type admits a mathematically-integral literal such as 1.0; the CI instance scan (float-rejecting JSON parse, see VERSIONING.md) closes that remaining lexical gap. |

## `chain/v1` — `spec/schemas/chain.v1.schema.json`

Tamper-evidence seal of a bundle: chain.json, written ONCE at clean finalize (its PRESENCE is the primary completeness marker). Two linear hash chains run over the bundle: 'events' (each events.jsonl line) and 'decisions' (each decisions/NNNN.json file's bytes). Links are appended incrementally to chain.jsonl (one chain_link/v1 line per chained record, fsynced with its record) so a kill -9 at any point leaves a fully verifiable prefix (SCH-3, C3.1). Linear chains, not Merkle: V1 verification is always whole-prefix, and per-record links localize tampering exactly - the first seq where a recomputed hash diverges NAMES the record; the protocol doc's Merkle commitments are Phase-2 multi-party machinery that can wrap this root later without changing any record format. Genesis binds run identity, pack, agent, and config, so a chain cannot be transplanted between runs. Verification always operates on STORED BYTES, never on re-encoded parsed objects. Verifier verdict is three-valued: COMPLETE / TRUNCATED / CORRUPT - never a boolean.

| Field path | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | const `"chain/v1"` | required | Schema name and major version of this document (the seal). Lines of chain.jsonl use $defs/chain_link with schema 'chain_link/v1'. |
| `run_id` | string | required | Run this seal covers (matches bundle_manifest.run_id). |
| `streams` | object | required | Per-stream chain summary. Genesis (per stream) = SHA-256 of JCS({schema:'chain_genesis/v1', stream, run_id, pack_content_hash, agent_manifest_sha256, run_config_sha256}) where run_config_sha256 = SHA-256 of JCS(bundle_manifest.run_config). Link i = SHA-256 of JCS({schema:'chain_link/v1', stream, seq: i, record_sha256: h_i, prev: link_(i-1)}) with prev = genesis for i = 0. |
| `streams.events` | ref: `stream_head` | required | Head of the events.jsonl hash chain (see $defs/stream_head). |
| `streams.decisions` | ref: `stream_head` | required | Head of the decisions/ record hash chain (see $defs/stream_head). |
| `files` | object (map) | required | Whole-file content addresses of every non-chained bundle file (manifests, ledgers, metrics, chain.jsonl itself): bundle-relative path -> SHA-256 over the complete uncompressed bytes. These files are pure derivations of the chained streams + pack, so content-addressing (not per-record chaining) suffices. |
| `files.*` | string | map value | SHA-256 of the file's uncompressed bytes. |
| `blobs` | object | required | Counts of content-addressed blob stores. Individual blob hashes are already committed inside chained events (ObservationEmitted.observation_sha256, AgentResponded.raw_sha256), so only counts are needed here. Under the share redaction profile, raw/ blobs may be deleted; the chain remains valid and redaction.json lists the absences. |
| `blobs.observations` | object | required | observations/NNNN.json store. |
| `blobs.observations.count` | integer | required | Number of stored observation files (= turns). |
| `blobs.raw` | object | required | raw/NNNN-aK.txt store. |
| `blobs.raw.count` | integer | required | Number of stored raw response files (attempts across all turns). |
| `complete` | boolean | required | True iff finalize succeeded and the final event is EpisodeEnd. chain.json only exists on clean finalize, so this is true in practice; a crashed run has NO chain.json and verifies as TRUNCATED from chain.jsonl alone. |
| `root` | string | required | The bundle's single publishable identity: SHA-256 over the JCS bytes of this document with the 'root' member removed. Printed on reports and share cards; a share sub-bundle names its parent by this value. |
| `$defs/stream_head` | object | definition | Summary of one linear hash chain. |
| `$defs/stream_head.genesis` | string | required | Genesis link value binding the chain to run identity, pack content hash, agent manifest, and run config. |
| `$defs/stream_head.head` | string | required | Final link value after the last record. |
| `$defs/stream_head.count` | integer | required | Number of chained records (events: lines; decisions: files). |
| `$defs/chain_link` | object | definition | One line of chain.jsonl, appended and fsynced together with its record so the surviving prefix of a crashed run is fully verifiable. |
| `$defs/chain_link.schema` | const `"chain_link/v1"` | required | Schema name and major version of this line. |
| `$defs/chain_link.stream` | enum: `"events"` \| `"decisions"` | required | Which chain this link extends. |
| `$defs/chain_link.seq` | integer | required | 0-based position: event seq, or decision turn index. |
| `$defs/chain_link.record_sha256` | string | required | SHA-256 of the record's stored bytes (JSONL line excluding its terminating newline; decision file: whole file bytes). |
| `$defs/chain_link.link_sha256` | string | required | This link's value: SHA-256 of JCS({schema:'chain_link/v1', stream, seq, record_sha256, prev}) where prev is the previous link value (genesis for seq 0). Stored so verification can restart from any prefix point. |

## `decision_record/v1` — `spec/schemas/decision_record.v1.schema.json`

The product: one legible per-turn audit record at decisions/NNNN.json (NNNN = zero-padded 4-digit turn index; every turn gets a record, INCLUDING missed/timeout turns, so the NNNN<->turn mapping is total and gap-free). It is a MATERIALIZED DERIVED VIEW over events.jsonl, assembled by a pure function of the event stream: every field must byte-equal its source event payloads (the replay verifier regenerates records from events and diffs; on conflict, events win). Deliberately denormalized: an auditor opens ONE file and reads the whole story - saw, said, meant, rules, happened, cost to hold, account after.

| Field path | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | const `"decision_record/v1"` | required | Schema name and major version of this document. |
| `run_id` | string | required | Run this record belongs to (matches bundle_manifest.run_id). |
| `turn` | integer | required | Decision-turn index; equals the NNNN of this file's name. |
| `bar_index` | integer | required | Decision bar observed (at its close) this turn. |
| `ts` | integer | required | Virtual clock at observation emission, REAL UTC epoch-milliseconds (bundle side; only observations are rebased). |
| `saw` | object | required | WHAT THE AGENT SAW: content address of the exact canonical observation; full bytes stored in-bundle at the ref (SCH-5 'from stored data alone'). |
| `saw.observation_sha256` | string | required | SHA-256 of the JCS observation bytes; must equal ObservationEmitted.observation_sha256 and the hash of the stored file. |
| `saw.observation_ref` | string | required | Bundle-relative path, e.g. 'observations/0007.json'. |
| `said` | object | required | WHAT THE AGENT SAID: every attempt, verbatim via content address. Empty attempts array = no response at all (timeout/unreachable); the absence is itself evidence. |
| `said.attempts` | array of object | required | One entry per IC-6 attempt, in order, including malformed ones. |
| `said.attempts[].attempt` | enum: `1` \| `2` | required | Attempt number. |
| `said.attempts[].raw_ref` | string | required | Bundle-relative path of the verbatim response bytes, e.g. 'raw/0007-a1.txt'. Under the share redaction profile the file may be absent (listed in redaction.json); the hash still verifies what was said. |
| `said.attempts[].raw_sha256` | string | required | SHA-256 of the verbatim response bytes. |
| `said.attempts[].raw_bytes` | integer | required | Byte length of the response. |
| `said.attempts[].latency_ms` | integer | required | Harness-measured wall latency for this attempt (recorded, never consumed). |
| `said.attempts[].http_status` | integer \| null | required | HTTP status; null for in-process adapters. |
| `said.attempts[].token_usage` | object \| null | required | Agent-reported token usage; null when unavailable. |
| `said.attempts[].token_usage.input_tokens` | integer | required | Reported input tokens. |
| `said.attempts[].token_usage.output_tokens` | integer | required | Reported output tokens. |
| `said.attempts[].transport` | enum: `"http"` \| `"in_process"` | required | Adapter used. |
| `meant` | object | required | WHAT THE AGENT MEANT: exactly one of action/rejected is non-null, discriminated by status. The cross-field coupling is SCHEMA-ENFORCED by the allOf/if/then pair below (a record with status 'parsed' and action null is schema-invalid, not merely doc-invalid). Missed decisions (timeout/agent_error) are status 'rejected' with the corresponding reason (SAFE-4). |
| `meant.status` | enum: `"parsed"` \| `"rejected"` | required | parsed => action non-null, rejected null; rejected => the reverse. |
| `meant.action` | object \| null | required | Canonical parsed action (mirror of ActionParsed payload), or null. The leverage payload (target_lev_1e4, max_slippage_bps) is conditionally required behind intent_kind (allOf/if/then), mirroring the ActionParsed seam: intent_kind is required whenever action is non-null and its sole v1 member is 'leverage_target', so every v1 record still carries the full leverage vector; a future commerce intent kind is a MINOR bump (new enum member + own conditional branch). The keywords are vacuous when action is null (required/properties constrain objects only), so the null branch is unaffected. |
| `meant.action.intent_kind` | enum: `"leverage_target"` | required | Canonical intent discriminator, mirror of ActionParsed.intent_kind (the IC-3 seam); constant 'leverage_target' in v1, additive-tolerant (VERSIONING.md) so a future commerce intent kind is a minor bump. |
| `meant.action.target_lev_1e4` | object (map) | conditional | Market alias -> signed target leverage, 1e-4 units. |
| `meant.action.target_lev_1e4.*` | integer | map value | Signed target leverage in 1e-4 units. |
| `meant.action.max_slippage_bps` | integer \| null | conditional | Slippage tolerance in bps, or null. |
| `meant.action.from_attempt` | enum: `1` \| `2` | required | Attempt that produced the accepted action. |
| `meant.rejected` | object \| null | required | Mirror of the ActionRejected payload, or null. |
| `meant.rejected.reason` | enum: `"oversize"` \| `"invalid_json"` \| `"schema_invalid"` \| `"unknown_schema"` \| `"unknown_field"` \| `"unknown_market"` \| `"invalid_target_format"` \| `"float_target"` \| `"target_out_of_range"` \| `"invalid_slippage"` \| `"timeout"` \| `"agent_error"` | required | Final failure reason from the IC-3 validation table. |
| `meant.rejected.detail` | string | required | Deterministic diagnostic. |
| `meant.rejected.validator_error` | string \| null | required | Error text fed back on the retry, or null if none occurred. |
| `meant.rejected.attempts` | enum: `1` \| `2` | required | Attempts made. |
| `rules` | array of object | required | WHICH RULES RAN: every constraint verdict this turn, pass AND block (mirrors of RiskCheck payloads, in emission order). Empty exactly when no action was parsed (gates run only on parsed intents). |
| `rules[].constraint_id` | string | required | Constraint evaluated. |
| `rules[].constraint_type` | enum: `"leverage_cap_gross"` \| `"leverage_cap_market"` \| `"turnover_cap"` \| `"drawdown_kill_switch"` | required | Constraint semantics. |
| `rules[].scope` | string | required | Market alias or 'account'. |
| `rules[].observed` | integer | required | Value checked, in `unit` units. |
| `rules[].limit` | integer | required | Limit in force, in `unit` units. |
| `rules[].unit` | string | required | Unit of observed/limit. |
| `rules[].verdict` | enum: `"pass"` \| `"block"` | required | The conformance verdict. This enum is on the additive-tolerant list (VERSIONING.md): a future conformance outcome (e.g. step_up / requires_user_authorization) arrives as a minor bump, not a major. observed/limit are numeric-only in v1; a non-scalar conformance value (e.g. a matched-set member) arrives as an optional additive field (minor bump), documented in IC-4. |
| `happened` | object | required | WHAT EXECUTED: verbatim mirrors of this turn's OrderFilled/OrderCancelled/LiquidationTriggered/PostKillSwitchAttempt payloads. All empty/null on missed, rejected, or fully-blocked turns. |
| `happened.fills` | array of `OrderFilled` | required | OrderFilled payloads, in seq order, with full price decomposition. |
| `happened.cancels` | array of `OrderCancelled` | required | OrderCancelled payloads, in seq order. |
| `happened.liquidation` | (anyOf variants) | required | LiquidationTriggered payload if this turn's holding bar liquidated the position; else null. |
| `happened.post_kill_switch_attempt` | (anyOf variants) | required | PostKillSwitchAttempt payload if a non-flat target arrived after the kill switch; else null. |
| `cost_to_hold` | object | required | WHAT HOLDING COST over this turn's bar: funding flows plus margin state after the bar. The carrying-cost block (funding today; storage/subscription/interest in a commerce profile tomorrow). |
| `cost_to_hold.funding` | array of `FundingApplied` | required | FundingApplied payloads for settlements crossed during this turn's holding bar, in seq order. |
| `cost_to_hold.margin_after` | (anyOf variants) | required | MarginUpdate payload at the holding bar's close (includes min intra-bar distance-to-liquidation, the wick near-miss); null when flat all bar. |
| `account_after` | object | required | Account state after the turn's bar, with the delta-NAV attribution terms stored (not derived) so 'why did NAV drop this bar' is answered inline and the MATH-2 identity is checkable by a from-scratch script: d_nav == d_price_pnl + d_funding + d_fees + d_liq_penalty, exactly, in integer micro-units. |
| `account_after.nav_micro` | integer | required | NAV after the bar, micro-quote. |
| `account_after.cash_micro` | integer | required | Free cash after the bar, micro-quote. |
| `account_after.realized_pnl_micro` | integer | required | Cumulative realized PnL, micro-quote. |
| `account_after.d_nav_micro` | integer | required | NAV change over this turn's bar, micro-quote. INVARIANT (CI, MATH-2): equals the sum of the four attribution terms below. |
| `account_after.d_price_pnl_micro` | integer | required | Mark-to-market price PnL component, micro-quote. |
| `account_after.d_funding_micro` | integer | required | Funding component, micro-quote (negative = paid). |
| `account_after.d_fees_micro` | integer | required | Fee component, micro-quote (always <= 0). |
| `account_after.d_liq_penalty_micro` | integer | required | Liquidation penalty component, micro-quote (0 except the terminal bar). |
| `event_seq_range` | object | required | The contiguous events.jsonl seq range this record was derived from - the denormalization is auditable back to the primary stream. |
| `event_seq_range.first_seq` | integer | required | First event seq of this turn (its ObservationEmitted). |
| `event_seq_range.last_seq` | integer | required | Last event seq of this turn. |
| `ext` | object (map) | optional | Sanctioned extension point (see VERSIONING.md). Recorder-ignored, hashed as-is; values are constrained by schema to JCS-safe types with no fractional numbers ($defs/ext_value). |
| `$defs/ext_value` | (anyOf variants) | definition | JCS-safe extension value (DET-2): null, boolean, string, integer within the I-JSON exact range +/-(2^53-1), or arrays/objects of the same, recursively. A JSON number with a fractional part (e.g. 1.5) is schema-INVALID here - ext contents ride into hashed documents as-is, and no fractional number may enter a hashed document. Boundary note: JSON Schema's 'integer' type admits a mathematically-integral literal such as 1.0; the CI instance scan (float-rejecting JSON parse, see VERSIONING.md) closes that remaining lexical gap. |

## `event/v1` — `spec/schemas/event.v1.schema.json`

One line of events.jsonl (IC-4): the ordered, append-only, canonical PRIMARY record of a run. Decision records are a materialized view over this stream; on any conflict, events win. Each line is JCS-canonical, individually hashed, and chained (see chain/v1). Timestamps here are REAL UTC epoch-ms: bundles are trusted-side evidence and are not anonymized - only observations are. The payload is a typed union discriminated on `type` (closed enum per major version).

| Field path | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | const `"event/v1"` | required | Schema name and major version; present per-line because event lines are individually hashed/chained and may be extracted standalone. |
| `seq` | integer | required | Monotonic, contiguous, 0-based stream sequence number assigned by the recorder. THE total order; the chain and all tamper-naming key off seq. Gaps or duplicates = verification failure. |
| `ts` | integer | required | Virtual-clock time of the event, REAL UTC epoch-milliseconds. For harness-sourced events (EgressBlocked), the harness's copy of the virtual clock at receipt. |
| `turn` | integer \| null | required | Decision turn this event belongs to (turn n owns: its observation, responses, gates, next-bar-open fills, and the funding/margin flows of the holding bar), or null for run-scoped events (e.g. EpisodeEnd). |
| `bar_index` | integer \| null | required | Decision-bar index at emission, or null for pre/post-episode events. |
| `source` | enum: `"engine"` \| `"harness"` \| `"recorder"` | required | Emitting authority - an auditor must know whether the engine or the sandbox proxy witnessed the fact. Multi-party provenance is first-class (a future settlement processor is a new enum member, minor bump). |
| `type` | enum: `"ObservationEmitted"` \| `"AgentResponded"` \| `"ActionParsed"` \| `"ActionRejected"` \| `"RiskCheck"` \| `"OrderFilled"` \| `"OrderCancelled"` \| `"FundingApplied"` \| `"MarginUpdate"` \| `"NearLiquidation"` \| `"LiquidationTriggered"` \| `"KillSwitchTriggered"` \| `"PostKillSwitchAttempt"` \| `"EgressBlocked"` \| `"EpisodeEnd"` | required | Event type; closed V1 vocabulary (dev-plan names kept verbatim, including NearLiquidation added at the C0.3 reconciliation). New members are a minor bump; readers reject unknown types under the same major only if strict-mode, else ignore-with-warning. |
| `payload` | object | required | Type-specific body; validated by the oneOf discriminated union below. |
| `ext` | object (map) | optional | Sanctioned extension point (see VERSIONING.md). Engine-ignored, hashed as-is; values are constrained by schema to JCS-safe types with no fractional numbers ($defs/ext_value). |
| `$defs/ext_value` | (anyOf variants) | definition | JCS-safe extension value (DET-2): null, boolean, string, integer within the I-JSON exact range +/-(2^53-1), or arrays/objects of the same, recursively. A JSON number with a fractional part (e.g. 1.5) is schema-INVALID here - ext contents ride into hashed documents as-is, and no fractional number may enter a hashed document. Boundary note: JSON Schema's 'integer' type admits a mathematically-integral literal such as 1.0; the CI instance scan (float-rejecting JSON parse, see VERSIONING.md) closes that remaining lexical gap. |
| `$defs/sha256` | string | definition | Algorithm-prefixed lowercase-hex SHA-256 string. |
| `$defs/target_lev_map` | object (map) | definition | Canonical parsed target vector: market alias -> integer leverage in 1e-4 units. The only action representation that is ever hashed. |
| `$defs/target_lev_map.*` | integer | map value | Signed target leverage in 1e-4 units (15000 = 1.5x long, -15000 = 1.5x short, 0 = flat). |
| `$defs/ObservationEmitted` | object | definition | Turn start: binds the stored observation into the chain (WHAT THE AGENT SAW). Emitted once per turn even when a retry re-sends the identical observation. |
| `$defs/ObservationEmitted.observation_sha256` | ref: `sha256` | required | SHA-256 of the JCS bytes of the observation served this turn (equals the hash of observations/NNNN.json). |
| `$defs/ObservationEmitted.observation_ref` | string | required | Bundle-relative path of the stored observation, e.g. 'observations/0007.json'. |
| `$defs/AgentResponded` | object | definition | Each response received, including malformed ones (WHAT THE AGENT SAID). Raw text is content-addressed into raw/ rather than inlined, so share-profile redaction can delete the blob without breaking any chained record hash (SCH-3 x SCH-4). |
| `$defs/AgentResponded.attempt` | enum: `1` \| `2` | required | 1 = first ask; 2 = the single retry after a validation failure. |
| `$defs/AgentResponded.raw_ref` | string | required | Bundle-relative path of the verbatim response bytes, e.g. 'raw/0007-a1.txt'. |
| `$defs/AgentResponded.raw_sha256` | ref: `sha256` | required | SHA-256 of the verbatim response bytes; survives redaction (verifiable absence). |
| `$defs/AgentResponded.raw_bytes` | integer | required | Byte length of the verbatim response. |
| `$defs/AgentResponded.latency_ms` | integer | required | Harness-measured wall latency, request-sent to last-byte-received. Recorded, never consumed by any economic computation (outside the determinism domain). |
| `$defs/AgentResponded.http_status` | integer \| null | required | HTTP status code of the response; null for in-process adapters. |
| `$defs/AgentResponded.token_usage` | object \| null | required | Agent-self-reported token usage copied from action.usage; null when unavailable (explicit null, never absent). |
| `$defs/AgentResponded.token_usage.input_tokens` | integer | required | Reported input/prompt tokens. |
| `$defs/AgentResponded.token_usage.output_tokens` | integer | required | Reported output/completion tokens. |
| `$defs/AgentResponded.transport` | enum: `"http"` \| `"in_process"` | required | Adapter that carried this response. |
| `$defs/ActionParsed` | object | definition | Parse success (WHAT THE AGENT MEANT): the canonical integer form of the wire action. Free-text comment and usage telemetry are NOT copied here - they live in the content-addressed raw response. The leverage payload (target_lev_1e4, max_slippage_bps) is conditionally required behind intent_kind via the allOf/if/then above - the same seam as the wire form (action.v1). Because intent_kind is itself required here and its sole v1 member is 'leverage_target', every v1 canonical action still carries the full leverage vector (no behavior or byte change for trading); a future intent kind (e.g. commerce purchase_intent) adds its own enum member + conditional branch + optional payload properties - a MINOR bump on this hashed form, not an event/v2 major. |
| `$defs/ActionParsed.intent_kind` | enum: `"leverage_target"` | required | Canonical intent discriminator (the IC-3 seam): constant 'leverage_target' for every v1 trading action (wire absence canonicalizes to it), so it never varies within v1 and determinism is unaffected. On the additive-tolerant list (VERSIONING.md): a future intent kind (commerce purchase_intent) is a new enum member whose payload branch carries its own canonical fields - a MINOR bump instead of an action/v2 + event/v2 + chain-rippling major. |
| `$defs/ActionParsed.target_lev_1e4` | ref: `target_lev_map` | conditional | Canonical signed target-leverage vector (see $defs/target_lev_map); conditionally required behind intent_kind = leverage_target (always present in v1). |
| `$defs/ActionParsed.max_slippage_bps` | integer \| null | conditional | Slippage tolerance in integer bps; null when the agent omitted it (wire absence canonicalizes to null). |
| `$defs/ActionParsed.from_attempt` | enum: `1` \| `2` | required | Which IC-6 attempt produced the accepted action. |
| `$defs/ActionRejected` | object | definition | No valid action this turn after all attempts: parse/transport failure or timeout. Position unchanged - a rejection is data, not a crash (SAFE-2). Gate blocks are NOT rejections; they are RiskCheck{block} on a successfully parsed action. |
| `$defs/ActionRejected.reason` | enum: `"oversize"` \| `"invalid_json"` \| `"schema_invalid"` \| `"unknown_schema"` \| `"unknown_field"` \| `"unknown_market"` \| `"invalid_target_format"` \| `"float_target"` \| `"target_out_of_range"` \| `"invalid_slippage"` \| `"timeout"` \| `"agent_error"` | required | Final failure reason (of the last attempt), from the IC-3 validation table. timeout = no bytes within the deadline; agent_error = transport failure/crash/5xx. Both are missed decisions (SAFE-4). |
| `$defs/ActionRejected.detail` | string | required | Deterministic human-readable diagnostic template instantiated with the offending values. |
| `$defs/ActionRejected.validator_error` | string \| null | required | The exact validator error text fed back to the agent on the retry (attempt 2), or null if no retry occurred - the audit answer to 'was it warned?'. |
| `$defs/ActionRejected.attempts` | enum: `1` \| `2` | required | How many attempts were made (timeout/agent_error are never retried, so those record 1). |
| `$defs/RiskCheck` | object | definition | One conformance verdict for one constraint (WHICH RULES RAN). Emitted for EVERY active constraint whenever an action is parsed - pass AND block both recorded (SAFE-1 attempted-vs-executed). Any block => the whole action is blocked, position unchanged, never clamped. |
| `$defs/RiskCheck.constraint_id` | string | required | Constraint row evaluated (matches observation.risk.constraints[].constraint_id). |
| `$defs/RiskCheck.constraint_type` | enum: `"leverage_cap_gross"` \| `"leverage_cap_market"` \| `"turnover_cap"` \| `"drawdown_kill_switch"` | required | Constraint semantics (closed V1 enum, minor-bump extensible). |
| `$defs/RiskCheck.scope` | string | required | Market alias bound, or 'account'. |
| `$defs/RiskCheck.observed` | integer | required | The value checked (e.g. requested gross leverage, projected turnover), in `unit` units. |
| `$defs/RiskCheck.limit` | integer | required | The limit in force, in `unit` units. |
| `$defs/RiskCheck.unit` | string | required | Unit of observed/limit: 'lev_1e4', '1e8', or 'micro'. |
| `$defs/RiskCheck.verdict` | enum: `"pass"` \| `"block"` | required | The conformance verdict. This enum is on the additive-tolerant list (VERSIONING.md): a future third outcome (e.g. step_up / requires_user_authorization for commerce mandate flows) arrives as a minor bump, not a major. observed/limit are deliberately numeric-only in v1; a non-scalar conformance value (e.g. an observed merchant vs an allowed set) arrives as an optional additive payload field (minor bump) - documented seam, IC-4 design decision 9. |
| `$defs/OrderFilled` | object | definition | Next-bar-open execution (WHAT HAPPENED), with the fill price fully decomposed so 'why this price' is answerable without the engine. The stress_2x economic path is a stored re-simulation (ledger_stress_2x.jsonl), not a second event stream. |
| `$defs/OrderFilled.market` | string | required | Market alias (resolve to venue instrument via the pack manifest). |
| `$defs/OrderFilled.side` | enum: `"buy"` \| `"sell"` | required | Fill side. |
| `$defs/OrderFilled.requested_qty_base_1e8` | integer | required | Quantity requested by the target-delta, 1e-8 base units, before caps/rounding. |
| `$defs/OrderFilled.qty_base_1e8` | integer | required | Quantity actually filled, 1e-8 base units (rounded toward zero to qty_step; capped by participation). |
| `$defs/OrderFilled.ref_open_px_ticks` | integer | required | Reference price: the next bar's trade-series open, ticks. |
| `$defs/OrderFilled.half_spread_ticks` | integer | required | Worst-side half-spread applied, in ticks (agent-adverse rounding). |
| `$defs/OrderFilled.impact_ticks` | integer | required | Impact term applied, in ticks (agent-adverse rounding). |
| `$defs/OrderFilled.fill_px_ticks` | integer | required | Effective fill price = ref_open +/- (half_spread + impact) against the taker, ticks. |
| `$defs/OrderFilled.notional_micro` | integer | required | Fill notional = qty x fill price, micro-quote. |
| `$defs/OrderFilled.fee_micro` | integer | required | Taker fee charged, micro-quote, rounded up (agent-adverse). |
| `$defs/OrderFilled.slippage_1e8` | integer | required | (fill_px - ref_open)/ref_open signed, in 1e-8 units (1 bp = 10000; bps derivable exactly). Compared against the agent's max_slippage_bps x 10000. |
| `$defs/OrderFilled.cost_profile` | const `"primary"` | required | Cost profile of this event stream. Always 'primary'; the stress profile is a stored ledger re-simulation (MATH-5). |
| `$defs/OrderCancelled` | object | definition | Whole or partial cancellation. A participation-cap partial produces one OrderFilled (filled part) AND one OrderCancelled (excess) in the same turn; excess is never filled later (MATH-7). |
| `$defs/OrderCancelled.market` | string | required | Market alias. |
| `$defs/OrderCancelled.reason` | enum: `"participation_cap"` \| `"min_notional"` \| `"max_slippage_exceeded"` \| `"qty_rounding"` | required | Why: exceeded participation cap; below min notional; modeled slippage above the agent's max_slippage_bps; or quantity rounded to zero at qty_step. |
| `$defs/OrderCancelled.requested_qty_base_1e8` | integer | required | Quantity requested, 1e-8 base units. |
| `$defs/OrderCancelled.cancelled_qty_base_1e8` | integer | required | Quantity cancelled (the whole request, or the excess over the cap), 1e-8 base units. |
| `$defs/OrderCancelled.detail` | string | required | Deterministic structured diagnostic (e.g. cap value, bar volume, computed slippage) rendered from a fixed template. |
| `$defs/FundingApplied` | object | definition | One venue settlement stamp crossed while holding (COST TO HOLD). Notional = position x INDEX price x rate - index, never mark or trade (MATH-4); the three-series separation is visible in the record itself. |
| `$defs/FundingApplied.market` | string | required | Market alias. |
| `$defs/FundingApplied.settlement_ts` | integer | required | Settlement instant, REAL UTC epoch-ms. |
| `$defs/FundingApplied.rate_1e8` | integer | required | Settled rate in 1e-8 units, era cap applied; positive = longs pay. |
| `$defs/FundingApplied.index_px_ticks` | integer | required | Index price at settlement, ticks. |
| `$defs/FundingApplied.position_qty_base_1e8` | integer | required | Signed position held through the settlement, 1e-8 base units. |
| `$defs/FundingApplied.amount_micro` | integer | required | Signed funding flow, micro-quote; negative = agent paid (agent-adverse rounding on the division). |
| `$defs/MarginUpdate` | object | definition | Margin state per market: emitted at every bar close while a position is open, and after every fill, funding application, and liquidation. Fully specifies the dev-plan's '{...}' placeholder. min_intrabar_dist_to_liq records the closest approach on the wick - near-death evidence even when the close was safe. |
| `$defs/MarginUpdate.market` | string | required | Market alias. |
| `$defs/MarginUpdate.mark_px_ticks` | integer | required | Mark-price close of the bar, ticks (margin/uPnL/liquidation all price off mark). |
| `$defs/MarginUpdate.mark_high_ticks` | integer | required | Mark-series intra-bar high, ticks (short-side liquidation check input, MATH-3). |
| `$defs/MarginUpdate.mark_low_ticks` | integer | required | Mark-series intra-bar low, ticks (long-side liquidation check input, MATH-3). |
| `$defs/MarginUpdate.position_qty_base_1e8` | integer | required | Signed position size, 1e-8 base units. |
| `$defs/MarginUpdate.entry_px_ticks` | integer \| null | required | Volume-weighted entry price, ticks; null when flat. |
| `$defs/MarginUpdate.margin_micro` | integer | required | Isolated margin allocated, micro-quote. |
| `$defs/MarginUpdate.maintenance_margin_micro` | integer | required | Maintenance margin required at current notional and tier, micro-quote. |
| `$defs/MarginUpdate.upnl_micro` | integer | required | Unrealized PnL at mark, micro-quote. |
| `$defs/MarginUpdate.liq_px_ticks` | integer \| null | required | Liquidation trigger price, ticks; null when flat. |
| `$defs/MarginUpdate.dist_to_liq_1e8` | integer \| null | required | \|mark_close - liq_px\|/mark_close in 1e-8 units (floor); null when flat. |
| `$defs/MarginUpdate.min_intrabar_dist_to_liq_1e8` | integer \| null | required | Minimum distance-to-liquidation reached on the bar's mark wick, 1e-8 units; null when flat. The near-miss number. |
| `$defs/NearLiquidation` | object | definition | The holding bar's adverse mark extreme came within the near-liquidation threshold (5% in V1) of the liquidation price WITHOUT crossing it (a cross emits LiquidationTriggered instead). Feeds the near-death timeline (C5.1); added to IC-4 at the C0.3 reconciliation. |
| `$defs/NearLiquidation.market` | string | required | Market alias. |
| `$defs/NearLiquidation.trigger` | enum: `"mark_high"` \| `"mark_low"` | required | Which mark extreme approached: high threatens shorts, low threatens longs. |
| `$defs/NearLiquidation.mark_extreme_px_ticks` | integer | required | The adverse mark extreme of the bar (low for longs, high for shorts), ticks. |
| `$defs/NearLiquidation.liq_px_ticks` | integer | required | The liquidation trigger price that was approached, ticks. |
| `$defs/NearLiquidation.min_intrabar_dist_to_liq_1e8` | integer | required | Closest approach: \|extreme - liq_px\| / extreme as a 1e-8 fraction (floor). Below threshold_1e8 by construction of this event. |
| `$defs/NearLiquidation.threshold_1e8` | integer | required | Near-liquidation threshold in 1e-8 units (V1: 5000000 = 5%). |
| `$defs/LiquidationTriggered` | object | definition | Intra-bar mark high/low breached the liquidation price (including gap-through). Terminal: the episode ends after bookkeeping (MATH-3). |
| `$defs/LiquidationTriggered.market` | string | required | Market alias. |
| `$defs/LiquidationTriggered.trigger` | enum: `"mark_high"` \| `"mark_low"` | required | Which mark extreme breached: high liquidates shorts, low liquidates longs. |
| `$defs/LiquidationTriggered.trigger_px_ticks` | integer | required | The breaching mark extreme, ticks. |
| `$defs/LiquidationTriggered.liq_px_ticks` | integer | required | The liquidation trigger price that was crossed, ticks. |
| `$defs/LiquidationTriggered.close_px_ticks` | integer | required | Forced-close execution price: the CONSERVATIVE side of the triggering bar, ticks. |
| `$defs/LiquidationTriggered.position_qty_base_1e8` | integer | required | Signed position liquidated, 1e-8 base units. |
| `$defs/LiquidationTriggered.penalty_micro` | integer | required | Liquidation penalty charged on liquidated notional, micro-quote. |
| `$defs/LiquidationTriggered.loss_micro` | integer | required | Total realized loss of the liquidation including penalty, micro-quote (negative = loss). |
| `$defs/KillSwitchTriggered` | object | definition | Episode drawdown limit (20%) breached: engine force-flattens all positions and keeps observing; further non-flat targets are blocked and recorded (SAFE-3). |
| `$defs/KillSwitchTriggered.drawdown_1e8` | integer | required | Peak-to-current NAV drawdown fraction in 1e-8 units at trigger. |
| `$defs/KillSwitchTriggered.limit_1e8` | integer | required | The configured limit (20000000 = 20%). |
| `$defs/KillSwitchTriggered.peak_nav_micro` | integer | required | Episode peak NAV, micro-quote. |
| `$defs/KillSwitchTriggered.nav_micro` | integer | required | NAV at trigger, micro-quote. |
| `$defs/KillSwitchTriggered.flatten_order_seqs` | array of integer | required | seq numbers of the forced flattening OrderFilled events (ordinary fills, referenced not duplicated). |
| `$defs/PostKillSwitchAttempt` | object | definition | A non-flat target arrived after the kill switch fired. The attempt itself is discipline evidence (SAFE-1/SAFE-3), recorded alongside its RiskCheck{drawdown-ks, block}. |
| `$defs/PostKillSwitchAttempt.target_lev_1e4` | ref: `target_lev_map` | required | The attempted (blocked) signed target-leverage vector (see $defs/target_lev_map) - the violation itself is evidence. |
| `$defs/PostKillSwitchAttempt.raw_sha256` | ref: `sha256` | required | Content address of the verbatim response that carried the attempt. |
| `$defs/EgressBlocked` | object | definition | The sandbox refused a network egress attempt from the agent container (ISO-2). source = 'harness'. Reports flag these as safety events. |
| `$defs/EgressBlocked.destination` | string | required | Destination as observed: domain, DNS name, or IP literal. |
| `$defs/EgressBlocked.port` | integer \| null | required | Destination port; null when not applicable (e.g. DNS query name block). |
| `$defs/EgressBlocked.protocol` | enum: `"https"` \| `"dns"` \| `"tcp"` \| `"udp"` \| `"other"` | required | Protocol class of the refused attempt. |
| `$defs/EgressBlocked.count` | integer | required | Coalesced repeat count of identical attempts within the turn. |
| `$defs/EpisodeEnd` | object | definition | Always the last event of a complete stream - the in-band completeness sentinel: a stream without EpisodeEnd is truncated (SCH-3). |
| `$defs/EpisodeEnd.reason` | enum: `"completed"` \| `"liquidated"` \| `"aborted"` | required | completed = window exhausted; liquidated = terminal liquidation; aborted = operator/pre-flight abort before or during the run. |
| `$defs/EpisodeEnd.final_turn` | integer \| null | required | Last decision-turn index, or null if aborted before turn 0. |
| `$defs/EpisodeEnd.final_nav_micro` | integer | required | Final NAV, micro-quote. |
| `$defs/EpisodeEnd.metrics_sha256` | ref: `sha256` | required | Hash of metrics.json as finalized. |

## `funding_row/v1` — `spec/schemas/funding_row.v1.schema.json`

One settled funding print as a JSONL line in a pack's funding.jsonl. Rows carry no per-row schema field (bulk-data exception; the file's schema is declared in pack_manifest.files[]). Deviation from the dev-plan sketch {ts, rate_1e8}: available_at is added so that ONE uniform point-in-time rule (available_at <= virtual clock) covers every observable row type with no per-type special case (ISO-1).

| Field path | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ts` | integer | required | Settlement instant, UTC epoch-milliseconds, venue-accurate (00/08/16 UTC for V1 Binance BTCUSDT). Pack validators assert stamps land exactly on the market's declared settlement offsets. |
| `available_at` | integer | required | Instant the print becomes observable. Always equal to ts (a funding rate is knowable the instant it settles); present so the ISO-1 filter is one mechanical rule over all row types. Pack validators assert available_at == ts. |
| `rate_1e8` | integer | required | Settled funding rate in 1e-8 units, signed; positive = longs pay shorts. Era cap already applied as recorded by the venue: \|rate_1e8\| <= the market's funding.cap_1e8 (2020-era Binance: 300000 = 0.30%; the COVID 2020-03-13 08:00 print sits exactly at -300000). |

## `ledger_row/v1` — `spec/schemas/ledger_row.v1.schema.json`

One line of ledger.jsonl (primary cost profile) or ledger_stress_2x.jsonl (2x cost-profile re-simulation of the SAME recorded action trace - stored data, not an in-memory derivation, so MATH-5/MATH-6 checks run on bytes): bar-by-bar account state with the delta-NAV attribution terms STORED, not derived. NORMATIVE INVARIANT (CI, MATH-2): nav_micro[i] - nav_micro[i-1] == d_price_pnl_micro + d_funding_micro + d_fees_micro + d_liq_penalty_micro, exactly, in integer micro-units, every bar; cash changes only by realized components, to the unit. The ledger IS the equity curve; metrics.json references it rather than duplicating it.

| Field path | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ts` | integer | required | Bar close, REAL UTC epoch-milliseconds (bundle side). |
| `bar_index` | integer | required | Decision-bar index of this row. |
| `turn` | integer \| null | required | Decision-turn index whose holding bar this row closes (bar k, k >= 1, is turn k-1's holding bar). Null ONLY for the bar-0 opening row, which no turn's holding bar closes: it seeds the equity curve at run_config.starting_nav_micro with all four delta terms zero. |
| `profile` | enum: `"primary"` \| `"stress_2x"` | required | Cost profile of this row's simulation (matches the containing file). |
| `nav_micro` | integer | required | Net asset value at bar close, micro-quote. |
| `cash_micro` | integer | required | Free cash at bar close, micro-quote. |
| `realized_pnl_micro` | integer | required | Cumulative realized PnL including funding and fees since episode start, micro-quote. |
| `d_nav_micro` | integer | required | NAV change over this bar, micro-quote. INVARIANT: equals the sum of the four attribution terms below, exactly. |
| `d_price_pnl_micro` | integer | required | Mark-to-market price PnL component of the bar's NAV change, micro-quote. |
| `d_funding_micro` | integer | required | Funding component, micro-quote (negative = paid). |
| `d_fees_micro` | integer | required | Fee component, micro-quote (always <= 0). |
| `d_liq_penalty_micro` | integer | required | Liquidation penalty component, micro-quote (0 except the terminal bar). |
| `positions` | object (map) | required | Map: market alias -> position state at bar close. Per-market ledger from day one (multi-asset shape, Scope section 2). Flat markets appear with qty 0 and null price fields. |
| `positions.*` | object | map value | One market's position state at bar close (the value of each positions map entry). |
| `positions.*.qty_base_1e8` | integer | required | Signed position size, 1e-8 base units. |
| `positions.*.entry_px_ticks` | integer \| null | required | Volume-weighted entry price, ticks; null when flat. |
| `positions.*.mark_px_ticks` | integer | required | Mark-price close of the bar, ticks. |
| `positions.*.upnl_micro` | integer | required | Unrealized PnL at mark, micro-quote. |
| `positions.*.margin_micro` | integer | required | Isolated margin allocated, micro-quote. |
| `positions.*.maintenance_margin_micro` | integer | required | Maintenance margin required, micro-quote. |
| `positions.*.liq_px_ticks` | integer \| null | required | Liquidation trigger price, ticks; null when flat. |
| `positions.*.dist_to_liq_1e8` | integer \| null | required | Distance to liquidation as a 1e-8 fraction of mark; null when flat. |

## `metrics/v1` — `spec/schemas/metrics.v1.schema.json`

Final metrics of a run, both cost profiles in one document. CI rule (MATH-5, mechanical): the key sets of profiles.primary and profiles.stress_2x are IDENTICAL by schema construction - 'no headline exists only under the optimistic cost profile' becomes a set-equality check. Metric vocabulary is survival-native (LABEL-3): returns AND drawdown/CVaR/distance-to-liquidation percentiles. All ratio metrics are integer fixed-point 1e-8 with floor (toward -infinity) rounding on division, estimator fine print pinned in spec/metrics.md and worked examples in the golden fixture (C0.3); this document is hashed, so the no-floats rule applies. The per-bar equity curve is NOT duplicated here: ledger.jsonl IS the equity curve (one source of truth per number).

| Field path | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | const `"metrics/v1"` | required | Schema name and major version of this document. |
| `run_id` | string | required | Run these metrics summarize. |
| `claim_label` | const `"survival-stress"` | required | Propagated verbatim from the pack manifest so report/share generators cannot lose it (LABEL-1): scenario evidence is survival/stress evidence, never skill/alpha. |
| `profiles` | object | required | Per-cost-profile metrics; both profiles mandatory with the identical key set. |
| `profiles.primary` | ref: `profile_metrics` | required | Metrics computed under the primary (1x) cost profile (see $defs/profile_metrics). |
| `profiles.stress_2x` | ref: `profile_metrics` | required | Metrics recomputed under the doubled-cost stress profile (see $defs/profile_metrics). |
| `profile_invariant` | object | required | Counts and verdicts independent of the cost profile. |
| `profile_invariant.bars` | integer | required | Decision bars simulated. |
| `profile_invariant.turns` | integer | required | Decision turns (= decision records). |
| `profile_invariant.invalid_actions` | integer | required | Turns ending in ActionRejected for a parse/validation reason. |
| `profile_invariant.missed_decisions` | integer | required | Turns ending in ActionRejected{timeout\|agent_error} (SAFE-4). |
| `profile_invariant.gate_blocks` | integer | required | RiskCheck events with verdict 'block'. |
| `profile_invariant.post_kill_switch_attempts` | integer | required | PostKillSwitchAttempt events recorded. |
| `profile_invariant.egress_blocked_count` | integer | required | EgressBlocked events recorded (sum of coalesced counts). |
| `profile_invariant.liquidated` | boolean | required | True iff a LiquidationTriggered event occurred (terminal). |
| `profile_invariant.kill_switch_fired` | boolean | required | True iff the drawdown kill switch fired. |
| `profile_invariant.survival_verdict` | enum: `"survived"` \| `"liquidated"` \| `"killed_flat"` | required | The headline verdict: survived to window end; liquidated (terminal); or kill-switch-flattened and finished flat. |
| `$defs/profile_metrics` | object | definition | One cost profile's metric set. The required list IS the mandatory shared key set (additionalProperties false + identical required = MATH-5 by construction). |
| `$defs/profile_metrics.net_return_1e8` | integer | required | Net episode return (final NAV / starting NAV - 1) in 1e-8 units, floor rounding. |
| `$defs/profile_metrics.max_drawdown_1e8` | integer | required | Maximum peak-to-trough NAV drawdown fraction, 1e-8 units. |
| `$defs/profile_metrics.sortino_1e8` | integer | required | Sortino ratio in 1e-8 fixed point; estimator and rounding pinned in spec/metrics.md. |
| `$defs/profile_metrics.cvar5_1e8` | integer | required | CVaR(5%) of per-bar returns, 1e-8 units (negative = loss). |
| `$defs/profile_metrics.funding_paid_micro` | integer | required | Net funding flow over the episode, micro-quote (negative = paid). |
| `$defs/profile_metrics.fees_paid_micro` | integer | required | Total fees paid, micro-quote (always <= 0). |
| `$defs/profile_metrics.fill_cost_micro` | integer | required | Total spread+impact execution cost versus reference opens, micro-quote (always <= 0). |
| `$defs/profile_metrics.turnover_1e8` | integer | required | Gross traded notional / starting NAV, 1e-8 units. |
| `$defs/profile_metrics.dist_to_liq_min_1e8` | integer \| null | required | Minimum intra-bar distance-to-liquidation over the episode, 1e-8 units; null if never in position. |
| `$defs/profile_metrics.dist_to_liq_p05_1e8` | integer \| null | required | 5th percentile of bar-close distance-to-liquidation while in position; null if never in position. |
| `$defs/profile_metrics.dist_to_liq_p25_1e8` | integer \| null | required | 25th percentile of bar-close distance-to-liquidation while in position; null if never in position. |
| `$defs/profile_metrics.dist_to_liq_median_1e8` | integer \| null | required | Median bar-close distance-to-liquidation while in position; null if never in position. |
| `$defs/profile_metrics.equity_curve_ref` | string | required | Bundle-relative path of this profile's ledger file (the equity curve): 'ledger.jsonl' or 'ledger_stress_2x.jsonl'. |

## `observation/v1` — `spec/schemas/observation.v1.schema.json`

What the agent sees at one decision turn (IC-2). This is the ONLY anonymized surface in the system (ISO-3/ISO-4): every timestamp is REBASED epoch-ms (real time minus the largest whole-week multiple <= the pack window start, recorded operator-side in bundle_manifest.time_rebase_offset_ms and never observable by the agent). Week-aligned rebasing preserves time-of-day (funding settles at rebased 00/08/16) and weekday, but destroys the calendar date. Every row satisfies available_at <= clock_ts (ISO-1, property-tested against the pack). This object is JCS-canonicalized, SHA-256-hashed (ObservationEmitted.observation_sha256) and stored in full at observations/NNNN.json. NO ext extension point on this schema: the isolation surface is deliberately closed (any extension could carry dates or scenario names).

| Field path | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | const `"observation/v1"` | required | Schema name and major version of this document. |
| `episode` | object | required | Episode identity and progress. No dates, no event names, no venue names anywhere. |
| `episode.episode_id` | string | required | Opaque episode identifier, minted randomly by the harness per run and recorded in the bundle manifest. The ONLY episode identity the agent ever sees; derived from nothing scenario-related (ISO-4). |
| `episode.turn` | integer | required | 0-based decision-turn index; equals the decisions/NNNN.json index. Increments every turn including missed ones. |
| `episode.bar_index` | integer | required | 0-based index of the most recently CLOSED decision bar (whose close this observation is taken at), counted from the first post-warmup bar. Equals turn in V1 (one decision per decision bar). |
| `episode.bars_total` | integer | required | Total decision bars in the episode; with bars_remaining lets the agent reason about horizon without dates. |
| `episode.bars_remaining` | integer | required | Decision bars remaining after this one. |
| `episode.decision_bar_ms` | integer | required | Decision bar duration in milliseconds (14400000 = 4h, 3600000 = 1h). A duration, not an instant: reveals cadence, never era. |
| `episode.response_deadline_ms` | integer | required | Per-attempt response budget the harness enforces (IC-6). Told to the agent as basic procedural fairness, and so timeout evidence is unambiguous. |
| `clock_ts` | integer | required | Virtual clock at this decision point, REBASED epoch-milliseconds (< 1e11 by construction; real epoch values are ~1.7e12, which the CI observation scan uses as a leak detector). Every row in this observation satisfies available_at <= clock_ts (ISO-1). |
| `markets` | object (map) | required | Map: market alias -> market view. V1: exactly {'BTC': ...}. A scrubbed subset of the pack descriptor: units, caps, fees, funding schedule - no venue name, no venue symbols (ISO-3). |
| `position` | object (map) | required | Map: market alias -> current position state (post the previous bar's settlement). Every tradable market appears, flat markets with qty 0 and null price fields (explicit is auditable). |
| `position.*` | object | map value | One market's current position state as shown to the agent (the value of each position map entry). |
| `position.*.qty_base_1e8` | integer | required | Signed position size in 1e-8 base units; positive = long, 0 = flat. |
| `position.*.entry_px_ticks` | integer \| null | required | Volume-weighted entry price in ticks; null when flat (explicit null, never absent). |
| `position.*.upnl_micro` | integer | required | Unrealized PnL at the current MARK price (never trade price), micro-quote. ISO-1 single-mark invariant (IC-2 CI scan item 4): MUST be computed from the same provenance-checked mark row whose close populates markets.<alias>.last_mark_px_ticks - this scalar has no in-band available_at and an agent holding a known position can solve the mark back out of it, so a future mark here IS a price leak; CI recomputes it from in-band fields and requires exact equality. |
| `position.*.margin_micro` | integer | required | Isolated margin allocated to this position, micro-quote. |
| `position.*.liq_px_ticks` | integer \| null | required | Mark price at which liquidation triggers, in ticks; null when flat. |
| `position.*.dist_to_liq_1e8` | integer \| null | required | \|mark - liq_px\| / mark as a 1e-8 fraction (floor division) - the trader's single most important survival number; null when flat. Mark-derived: bound by the same ISO-1 single-mark invariant as upnl_micro (computed from the mark behind last_mark_px_ticks; CI-recomputed). |
| `account` | object | required | Account state in micro-quote units. |
| `account.nav_micro` | integer | required | Net asset value = cash + sum of position margin + unrealized PnL, micro-quote. Includes uPnL and is therefore mark-derived: bound by the ISO-1 single-mark invariant (IC-2 CI scan item 4) - computed from the same provenance-checked mark behind last_mark_px_ticks, CI-recomputed from in-band fields. |
| `account.cash_micro` | integer | required | Free collateral not allocated to margin, micro-quote. |
| `account.realized_pnl_micro` | integer | required | Cumulative realized PnL since episode start (price PnL + funding + fees + penalties), micro-quote. |
| `risk` | object | required | The active constraint mandate: every limit that will be evaluated against this turn's action, with current usage. Structurally an AP2-style mandate (id + type + scope + limit + used + unit). Commerce extensibility, stated precisely (DECISIONS #5): SCALAR-budget constraint types (e.g. spend_cap - integer limit/used in `unit`) arrive as new rows via a minor `type` vocabulary bump with zero shape change; SET/EQUALITY constraint types (e.g. merchant_allowlist) additionally need an optional value-set field on the constraint row - a minor ADDITIVE bump under the versioning policy, but a schema change, not just a new row. |
| `risk.constraints` | array of object | required | One row per active constraint. Every RiskCheck event references a constraint_id from this list. |
| `risk.constraints[].constraint_id` | string | required | Stable identifier referenced by RiskCheck verdicts, e.g. 'lev-gross', 'lev-BTC', 'turnover', 'drawdown-ks'. |
| `risk.constraints[].type` | enum: `"leverage_cap_gross"` \| `"leverage_cap_market"` \| `"turnover_cap"` \| `"drawdown_kill_switch"` | required | Constraint semantics. Closed V1 enum, additive-tolerant (VERSIONING.md). Scalar commerce types (spend_cap) arrive by minor vocabulary bump alone; set/equality types (merchant_allowlist) also require an optional value-set row field (minor additive bump - see the risk block description). |
| `risk.constraints[].scope` | string | required | Market alias this constraint binds, or 'account' for account-wide constraints. |
| `risk.constraints[].limit` | integer | required | Limit value, in `unit` units (e.g. 30000 lev_1e4 = 3x; 20000000 1e8 = 20% drawdown). |
| `risk.constraints[].used` | integer | required | Current consumption in `unit` units (gross leverage in force, drawdown consumed from peak, turnover used). limit - used = remaining budget. |
| `risk.constraints[].unit` | string | required | Unit of limit/used: 'lev_1e4', '1e8', or 'micro'. Per-row units keep constraint rows domain-neutral. |
| `risk.kill_switch_active` | boolean | required | True once the episode drawdown kill switch has fired; all further non-flat targets are blocked and recorded (PostKillSwitchAttempt), while observations continue (SAFE-3). |
| `$defs/market_view` | object | definition | Per-market data the agent may legitimately know: microstructure constants, fee it pays, its leverage cap, trade-bar lookback, funding schedule and prints, plus current mark/index closes (so mark-vs-trade divergence, the thing that liquidates you, is visible without full extra series - token economy). ISO-4 honesty note: the venue constants exposed here (funding cap/floor, taker fee, tick size, qty step, min notional) are ERA-ACCURATE pack data and therefore fingerprint the historical era independently of price action (e.g. +/-300000 funding cap = 2020-era Binance). This is a documented, accepted disclosure - a real trader knows the venue's parameters - handled as a labeling matter (LABEL-2) exactly like era recognition from price action; it is NOT treated as a leak. leverage_cap is the protocol's cap, not a venue fingerprint. |
| `$defs/market_view.tick_size_micro` | integer | required | Price tick in micro-quote; interprets every *_ticks value in this observation. |
| `$defs/market_view.qty_step_base_1e8` | integer | required | Quantity rounding step in 1e-8 base units; lets the agent predict fill rounding. |
| `$defs/market_view.min_notional_micro` | integer | required | Minimum order notional in micro-quote; smaller orders are cancelled - lets the agent predict min-notional cancels. |
| `$defs/market_view.taker_fee_rate_1e8` | integer | required | Taker fee rate the agent pays on every fill, 1e-8 of notional. |
| `$defs/market_view.leverage_cap_lev_1e4` | integer | required | This market's leverage cap in 1e-4 units (30000 = 3x). Duplicated from risk.constraints for locality. |
| `$defs/market_view.last_mark_px_ticks` | integer | required | Most recent MARK-price close in ticks. Mark is what liquidates positions; exposing its close lets the agent see mark-vs-trade divergence without a full second bar series. |
| `$defs/market_view.last_index_px_ticks` | integer | required | Most recent INDEX-price close in ticks. Index prices funding notional. |
| `$defs/market_view.bars` | array of object | required | Trade-price bars at the decision interval only (no mixed 1h/4h in one observation), oldest first, length = effective lookback (run_config override, else pack default). Timestamps rebased. |
| `$defs/market_view.bars[].ts` | integer | required | Bar open, REBASED epoch-ms. |
| `$defs/market_view.bars[].available_at` | integer | required | When this row became observable (bar close), REBASED epoch-ms. Kept in-band so the ISO-1 property (available_at <= clock_ts) is checkable on the stored observation itself. |
| `$defs/market_view.bars[].o` | integer | required | Open price, ticks. |
| `$defs/market_view.bars[].h` | integer | required | High price, ticks. |
| `$defs/market_view.bars[].l` | integer | required | Low price, ticks. |
| `$defs/market_view.bars[].c` | integer | required | Close price, ticks. |
| `$defs/market_view.bars[].v_base_1e8` | integer | required | Bar volume in 1e-8 base units; lets a capacity-aware agent anticipate the participation cap. |
| `$defs/market_view.funding` | object | required | Funding schedule and recent prints - the cost-to-hold block, computable in-band by the agent. |
| `$defs/market_view.funding.interval_ms` | integer | required | Funding interval for THIS market in milliseconds (per-market data field, never a constant - MATH-4). |
| `$defs/market_view.funding.next_settlement_ts` | integer | required | Next scheduled settlement, REBASED epoch-ms. Explicit so agents need not reverse-engineer the settlement clock. |
| `$defs/market_view.funding.cap_1e8` | integer | required | Venue funding-rate cap in 1e-8 units (observable: a real trader knows the venue's cap). |
| `$defs/market_view.funding.floor_1e8` | integer | required | Venue funding-rate floor in 1e-8 units. |
| `$defs/market_view.funding.prints` | array of object | required | Trailing settled funding prints, oldest first, count = effective funding lookback. Timestamps rebased; every ts <= clock_ts (a print is observable at settlement). |
| `$defs/market_view.funding.prints[].ts` | integer | required | Settlement time, REBASED epoch-ms. |
| `$defs/market_view.funding.prints[].rate_1e8` | integer | required | Settled rate in 1e-8 units, era cap applied; positive = longs pay shorts. |

## `pack_manifest/v1` — `spec/schemas/pack_manifest.v1.schema.json`

Manifest of one scenario pack (IC-1). The only pack file committed to the repo (DATA-5): series files are built locally from pinned upstream archives and verified against the hashes recorded here. Packs are versioned by content hash, not counters. Everything here is operator/bundle-side; none of it (pack_id, regime_description, venue, real dates) is ever serialized into an observation (ISO-3/ISO-4).

| Field path | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | const `"pack_manifest/v1"` | required | Schema name and major version of this document. |
| `pack_id` | string | required | Human-readable pack slug, e.g. 'covid-2020'. Operator-side only; never shown to the agent. |
| `content_hash` | string | required | The pack's version identity: SHA-256 over the JCS bytes of {"schema":"pack_content/v1","files":[{path,sha256,bytes,records}...]} with entries sorted by path. Referenced by bundle manifests and chain genesis; replay refuses a pack whose recomputed content hash differs (DET-6). |
| `venue` | string | required | Venue identifier, 'binance-um' in V1. Deliberately a string, not an enum: venues (later: merchants, payment rails) are data (commerce-extensibility hook). |
| `window` | object | required | The pack's real-time window. Real UTC epoch-ms here; observations are rebased (see observation/v1). |
| `window.start_ts` | integer | required | First bar open, UTC epoch-milliseconds. Also anchors the observation time-rebase offset: offset = largest whole multiple of 604800000 (one week) <= start_ts, recorded in bundle_manifest.time_rebase_offset_ms. |
| `window.end_ts` | integer | required | Window end, UTC epoch-milliseconds, exclusive. |
| `bar_intervals_ms` | array of enum: `3600000` \| `14400000` | required | All bar durations present as series files in this pack. |
| `decision_bar_ms` | enum: `3600000` \| `14400000` | required | Bar duration the episode loop steps on: 14400000 (4h, default packs) or 3600000 (1h, stress packs). One decision turn per bar of this size. |
| `warmup_bars` | integer | required | Decision bars at window start reserved as lookback context before turn 0; no decisions occur during warmup. Explicit so 'how much history did turn 0 legitimately see' is a stored fact, not an inference. |
| `markets` | object (map) | required | Map: agent-facing market alias (e.g. 'BTC') -> full per-market venue descriptor. The alias keeps LLM payloads small and venue identity out of observations (ISO-3); the descriptor binds it to a venue-qualified instrument. Multi-asset shaped from day one (Scope section 2); V1 packs carry exactly one entry. |
